text:
iola_pd: kicked off because we need a clear decision on phased admission for reserved pools. two customer asks landed: predictable admission for enterprise vs best-effort for self-serve. need default and how to expose controls.
mark_s: tl;dr: we can do tiered admission windows: guaranteed admission band (always-served until X% occupancy) + opportunistic band (best-effort, preemptable). customers want simple controls: opt into Guaranteed Tier or default Opportunistic.
kevin_eng: implementation outline:
- runtime introduces admission_zone per-tenant: GUARANTEED | OPPORTUNISTIC
- scheduler enforces guaranteed until pool_util >= reserved_threshold
- opportunistic requests can be queued, spilled, or routed to quantized fallback models
sample config:
```
pool_defaults:
  reserved_threshold_pct: 75
  admission_policy:
    default: OPPORTUNISTIC
    guaranteed_band_cutoff: 75
```

taylor_ops: ops concerns: preemption storms when many tenants are hard-guaranteed. need a fair preempt ordering and cooldown to avoid oscillations. Also telemetry: track preemptions/day and queue_time percentiles.
sara_sales: field note: several current pilots want a middle ground: small guaranteed "safety slab" (e.g., 5% of pool) plus opportunistic remainder. They will pay a small premium for the slab.
billing-bot: reminder: introducing "guaranteed" semantics likely requires contract language and a new billing SKU for guaranteed slab.
iola_pd: proposal A: default remains opportunistic, offer an add-on "guaranteed slab" per pool with configurable slab size. Proposal B: change default to include small safety slab for all paid customers.
mark_s: tradeoffs: A = minimal blast radius, easier rollout. B = better out-of-box experience but increases baseline cost and complexity in pricing.
kevin_eng: runtime complexity is moderate for both. Main work: admission flag per-tenant, preemption ordering, and metrics. Edge cases: cross-pool tenants and multi-region pools require deterministic tie-breaker.
taylor_ops: rollout plan suggestion:
1) implement admission flags behind FF + canary in one region
2) create preemption backoff & telemetry
3) pilot guaranteed-slab add-on with 3 customers
4) GA and docs
sara_sales: pilot success criteria: pilot customers see <2% unexpected throttles for guaranteed slab over 14d and accept pricing.
iola_pd: launch criteria for default change (if we choose B): must have pricing model, legal sign-off, and a 7d canary with synthetic traffic showing <5% capacity regression for other tenants.
mark_s: my recommendation: ship A (add-on guaranteed slab) first. concurrently run experiments with small default slab for paid tiers to measure economics.
kevin_eng: estimate: admission FF + metrics = 2 sprints; preemption fairness + canary = 1-2 sprints after. Billing SKU + contracts = parallel work 2-3 weeks.
billing-bot: note: for add-on SKU we need ledger mapping and invoice labeling. recommend read-only pilot billing estimates before charging.
iola_pd: owners: kevin=eng, taylor=ops, sara=sales, mark=product pricing. I'll draft the PRD and add action items to tracker.
sara_sales: I'll line up 3 pilot customers and prepare sales materials that clearly state "guaranteed slab is reclaimable only under declared emergency with 10m notice".
taylor_ops: will design preemption cooldown and synthetic tests.
kevin_eng: will post RFC for admission_zone and tie-breaker rules by EOD.
iola_pd: decision: proceed with Proposal A (guaranteed-slab add-on) as immediate deliverable; run experiments for default-slab in parallel. sync next week for RFC review. :thumbsup:
